title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendor, travel, templates
author: Sofia Reynolds
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard processes for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the canonical internal templates. It is intended for all employees and managers as the single reference for requesting access, making changes to production systems, handling company data, running procurements, onboarding vendors, and submitting travel/expense claims.

Scope and intent

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and approved external collaborators.
- Provides minimum required controls and the canonical functional flows. Teams may add risk-appropriate controls above these standards but must not weaken the baseline.
- Exceptions must be documented and approved as described in the Exceptions & escalation section.

1) Roles and ownership

| Area | Primary owner | Secondary owner | Review cadence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Access & permissions | Security & compliance | Eng Infra | Quarterly |
| Change management | Eng Platform | Eng SRE | Monthly |
| Data management | Security & compliance | Applied ML | Annually |
| Procurement & expenses | Finance & Legal | People Ops | Quarterly |
| Vendor management | Finance & Legal | Legal | Quarterly |
| Travel policy | People Ops | Finance | Annually |
| Templates & process library | People Ops | All teams | Continuous |

2) Access & permissions (RBAC baseline)

Intro: Access to systems is granted on a least-privilege and just-in-time basis. Access requests must include justification, duration (if temporary), and an approving manager.

Key controls and procedures:

- Role matrix: The canonical role-to-permission mapping is maintained in Security's RBAC spreadsheet (link above).
- Request flow: 1) Employee/contractor opens an access request via the Access Request form (internal template). 2) Manager approves, indicating business justification. 3) Security reviews for compliance-sensitive permissions (e.g., production DB write, KMS access). 4) Access is provisioned and automatically logged.
- Approval thresholds:
  1) Low-risk (dashboard, non-sensitive logs): manager approval.
  2) Medium-risk (staging infra, analytics datasets): manager + security reviewer.
  3) High-risk (production write, KMS/HSM, customer data exports): manager + security lead + business owner.
- Time-limited access: All elevated rights must include an expiration date (typical max 30 days). Re-requests require justification and re-approval.
- Quarterly access review: Owners run automated access reports; managers attest to the least-privilege status of their direct reports. Security enforces removals for inactive accounts (90+ days inactivity).
- Service accounts: Must be registered, owned, and rotated per the Secrets & KMS rotation schedule. Non-human credentials cannot be shared.

3) Change management (applies to infra, runtime, and customer-impacting services)

Goal: Ensure safe, auditable changes with minimal customer impact.

Change types and processes:

- Standard changes (low risk, routine): documented in a change ticket, peer-reviewed, automated tests pass, scheduled in a weekly deploy window. Manager-level approval.
- Significant changes (configuration affecting SLOs, model-serving kernel changes, database schema) : require a Change Request (CR) with rollback plan, risk assessment, and at least one SRE and one Product/Owner approval. Schedule a canary and phased rollout.
- Emergency changes: Allowed only when the incident runbook requires it. Every emergency change must be followed by a post-change review and RCA within 5 business days.

Mandatory change request checklist (to attach to CR ticket):
1) Description of change and components affected.
2) Business justification and expected impact.
3) Rollout plan (canary, percentage rollout, regions).
4) Rollback plan and test steps.
5) Monitoring & alerting thresholds to validate success.
6) Owners and contact information.

SLO/alert thresholds to mention in CRs (examples):
- API 99th percentile latency: baseline 150 ms; degrade threshold 300 ms (trigger rollback).
- Error rate: baseline <0.5% 5m; action threshold >1% for 5m.

4) Data management (classification, handling, retention)

Data classification:
- Public: data intended for public consumption.
- Internal: company operational data that is not PII or customer-sensitive.
- Confidential: employee PII, internal security artifacts.
- Customer-sensitive: regulated customer data, PII, or data under contract restrictions.

Handling requirements by class:
- Encryption: All Confidential and Customer-sensitive data must be encrypted at rest (KMS-managed) and in transit (TLS >=1.2).
- Access control: Principle of least privilege; access approved through the Access & permissions process.
- Storage & residency: Customer contracts take precedence. For customer-sensitive data with residency requirements, use approved private deployment options and follow the Data Residency runbook.
- Retention & deletion: Default retention is 3 years for Internal and 7 years for Financial/Legal records unless otherwise specified. Data deletion requests must follow the Data Deletion Procedure (see related_pages).

Data breach and incident handling:
1) If a data exfiltration or unauthorized access is suspected, notify Security immediately and open an incident.
2) Security coordinates containment, customer notifications (if required), and regulatory reporting.
3) Evidence preservation: snapshot systems, export logs, and collect chain-of-custody info.

5) Procurement & expenses

Principles: Transparency, competitive sourcing for >$10k purchases, segregation of duties, and clear approval levels.

Approval matrix (examples):
- <$500: employee/manager approval.
- $500 - $10,000: manager + Finance review.
- >$10,000: Finance + Legal + VP approval (or delegated exec).

Procurement flow:
1) Create a Purchase Request (PR) using the Procurement template. Include justification, budget code, supplier, and expected timeline.
2) Finance verifies budget and initiates purchase order where required.
3) For cloud or SaaS subscriptions, SRE/Platform reviews for technical fit.
4) Sign-off and PO issuance.
5) Upon receipt, Finance matches invoice to PO and marks as complete.

Expense policy highlights:
- Reimbursable expenses include business travel, approved client entertainment, and necessary equipment within policy limits.
- Receipts required for expenses >$25. Personal expenses must be clearly separated.
- Corporate card usage: follow the Corporate Card Guide; misuse can result in card suspension and disciplinary action.

6) Vendor management and onboarding

Vendor lifecycle steps:
1) Needs assessment and justification.
2) Vendor risk assessment (security posture, SOC/ISO certifications, data handling).
3) Legal/Finance contract review with standard terms (data protection addendum when needed).
4) Procurement creates PO and finance sets payment terms.
5) Onboarding checklist: technical onboarding, credentials, communication plan, and SLA expectations.

Key controls:
- High-risk vendors (have access to customer data or critical infra) require quarterly security attestations and annual contract review.
- Vendor access: limited to named accounts, timeboxed, and reviewed at least quarterly.
- Termination: data return/destruction clause must be enforced; IT revokes credentials and confirms deletion.

7) Travel policy (business travel and reimbursement)

Booking and approvals:
- All travel requires pre-approval via the Travel Request form. Manager approval required for airfare and lodging.
- Use preferred vendors and travel partners for negotiated rates. Exceptions require documented justification.

Per diem and reimbursable items:
- Meals: per diem up to $75/day domestic, up to $125/day international (adjust for high-cost cities with prior approval).
- Ground transportation: rideshares for safe transit; public transit preferred when practical.
- Lodging: standard room rate; upgrades require manager approval.

Safety and incident reporting:
- Employees traveling for work must share itinerary with their manager and People Ops.
- Security incidents while traveling must be reported immediately to Security and People Ops.

8) Internal templates and forms (canonical list)

The following templates live in the Templates library (link in related_pages) and must be used for the corresponding processes:
- Access Request form (access-request-template)
- Change Request (CR) template (change-request-template)
- Procurement Purchase Request (procurement-pr-template)
- Vendor Onboarding checklist (vendor-onboarding-template)
- Travel Request and Expense report (travel-request-template)
- Data Deletion Request (data-deletion-template)

Templates include field guidance, required approvals, and attachments. Using canonical templates ensures auditability and consistent metadata for automated reporting.

9) Exceptions, escalations, and governance

- Exceptions: Any deviation from these baseline policies requires an Exceptions Request form and approval from the policy owner and a designated approver (security or finance depending on domain). Exceptions must include duration, risk mitigation, and a review date.
- Escalation path: Manager -> Policy owner -> VP of function -> Legal/CTO as needed. Security incidents follow the Incident Response playbook.
- Audit & compliance: Owners run quarterly self-audits and remediate findings within 30 days. External audits (SOC/ISO) will be scheduled by Security/Finance as required by customer contracts.

10) Operationalizing & training

- Onboarding: People Ops incorporates an overview of these policies into new hire orientation.
- Quarterly training: Security and Finance run mandatory policy refreshers for owners and approvers.
- Automation: Where possible, flows are automated via internal tooling (access request provisioning, PO matching, vendor attestations) and logged centrally for reporting.

Revision history

- 2026-11-01: Document created (S. Reynolds).
- 2027-03-15: Updated procurement thresholds and vendor quarterly attestation requirement (reviewers: D. Kim, P. Shah, L. O'Connor).

Instructions for use

- Use the templates for all formal requests and attach the completed templates to tickets in Jira or the procurement system.
- Policy owners are responsible for keeping this page current and for publishing changes with a visible changelog.

Contact the People Ops policy owner for questions or to request process clarifications.
